dedupe_keys.name: measuring latency reduction and the digital divide of cloud edge datacenters martin and dogar ripe atlas measurements 2023

description: This 2023 study measures network latency to current and predicted cloud edge datacenters of three major cloud providers around the world, using the RIPE Atlas platform to reach cloud regions, AWS Local Zones and network optimisation services that shorten the path to the cloud edge. It analyses the resulting digital divide: inequality rises as the relative difference between users closest and farthest from cloud compute grows, it falls unfairly on lower-income census tracts in the United States, and is extended globally using night-time lights as a wealth proxy. It also shows that low Earth orbit satellite internet can help close the divide. Producer: Noah Martin and Fahad Dogar, submitted 11 April 2023. Coverage: global measurements plus US census tracts. Access: paper on arXiv; no measurement data link was read on the abstract page. Licence and cost: free to read; licence arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the paper; no open reuse licence). Caveats: only the abstract page was read, the edge datacenter locations were partly predicted, and the measurement dates are of 2023. Simulation uses: the latency and equity findings give inputs for siting and capacity-planning models of edge data centres. Related record: Azure global infrastructure geographies (data-azure-global-infrastructure-geographies).
